name: ketogenesis
description: Ketogenesis. Liver converts excess acetyl-CoA into ketone bodies that can be used by brain, heart, and muscle during fasting or low-carbohydrate states.

nodes.label: Acetyl-CoA
nodes.notes: From β-oxidation. Accumulates when TCA capacity is limited (low OAA).

nodes.label: HMG-CoA
nodes.notes: Same intermediate as in cholesterol synthesis, but mitochondrial isoform.

nodes.label: Acetoacetate
nodes.notes: Primary ketone body. Can be reduced to β-hydroxybutyrate or spontaneously decarboxylated.

nodes.label: β-Hydroxybutyrate
nodes.notes: Most abundant circulating ketone body. Preferred fuel for many tissues.

nodes.label: Acetone
nodes.notes: Volatile. Formed by spontaneous decarboxylation of acetoacetate. Exhaled.

edges.notes: Adds a third acetyl-CoA. Rate-influencing step under ketogenic conditions.
Cleaves HMG-CoA to acetoacetate + acetyl-CoA. Key ketogenic enzyme.
Reversible. Ratio of β-HB / AcAc reflects mitochondrial NADH/NAD⁺ ratio.
Non-enzymatic. Acetone is exhaled and accounts for the fruity odor in ketoacidosis.
